content: Johan and I have been realizing this channel is now very hard to keep up with, and propose splitting it into nightly-testing-mathlib, nightly-testing-batteries and nightly-testing-cslib, in the hope that the relevant people find it easier to pay attention to the parts they care about.

Also note that we have several pairs of topics here, e.g. leanchecker and leanchecker failure, which respectively carry the success and failure messages from a given bot.

This is set up this way so that you can mute the success stream! Please, if you hang out in nightly-testing (thank you!!!) but find it noisy, do remember to mute the success streams to keep it sane.

I think:

  • #nightly-testing > leanchecker
  • #nightly-testing > nanoda
  • #nightly-testing > mathlib test executable
  • #nightly-testing > Mathlib `lake update` success

are the relevant ones for now. Perhaps we should split more?

Kim Morrison said:

and propose splitting it into nightly-testing-mathlib, nightly-testing-batteries and nightly-testing-cslib

To do this split, I propose asking Claude to review all the relevant CI bots and generate a collection of PRs updating where they send their messages. Shall I do this? Perhaps @Bryan Gin-ge Chen or @Marcelo Lynch could do it more reliably?
I trust Claude to do the split. Presumably it's just a matter of searching for nightly-testing in every leanprover and leanprover-community repo and doing a search-and-replace?
What is the purpose of the success streams? Making sure the test doesn't just fall silent at some point?
I opened website#835 with some updates to the "tags and branches" page; let's update that after the split is done (reviews / additions there would also be appreciated!)

Sebastian Ullrich said:

What is the purpose of the success streams? Making sure the test doesn't just fall silent at some point?

Yes -- it's happened previously, of course.

  • https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/548
  • https://github.com/leanprover-community/leanprover-community.github.io/pull/836
I've merged all the PRs above except for the batteries and cslib ones.
I've merged the batteries one.
Can anyone stop the huge stream notification going on right now please?
@Kim Morrison
nightly-testing.mp4
Hmm, stopped.

It's not actually generating notifications, for you, is it?

For me I don't actually see anything: they show up in recent conversations, but already marked as read.

Options:

  1. Continue as is, and subscribed to nightly-testing deal with the remaining annoyance of clutter in their "recent conversations" list. (We're about half way through the move.)
  2. Continue, but without the notification messages in the new/old topics.
  3. Just abandon the remaining conversations where they were.
It is, though now that it's stopped I've managed to clear the ~500 unread messages it created using the inbox tab, it can clear a channel in one click
I think if it's one click to clean up (and this only affects subscribers to nightly-testing), then I'm inclined to go with option 1 and just get this done.

I'm fine with it but I'd like advance notice to unsubscribe from this channel first.
Although I don't see why not option 2, specifically without notice on the old topic. Notice on the new topic makes sense, especially since people aren't yet subscribed to mathlib-nightly-testing.
You're not actually getting a push notification, right? I was just planning to clear them all at the end.
I have do-not-disturb enabled so no, but I still find it spamming, it makes Zulip unusable because I always use the recent conversations page.
The messages on the old topics leave breadcrumbs about the move, in case there are links to these threads anywhere.
